name: Estrogen/hormone skin theories (DHT acne)

angle.text: Forum posters link DHT, steroids and estrogen to acne and discuss anti-androgen or estrogen approaches to clearer skin. Dermatology links androgens to sebum and acne, but the looksmaxxing-specific protocols lack dedicated studies.

summary: Forum theories tying acne to DHT, steroids and estrogen; androgens are linked to acne in dermatology, but looksmaxxing-specific claims lack dedicated studies.
note: Hormone-altering approaches carry medical risks; no studies of the community protocols found.
currentQuick:
Forum discussion links acne to DHT and steroids and proposes hormone-based fixes. Dermatology literature supports a role for androgens in acne.
The specific forum protocols have not been studied.
How it works: Androgens such as DHT increase sebum production, which is associated with acne.
Risks and caveats: Steroid use can cause acne; hormonal drugs have their own risks and are clinician-managed.
deepLead:
Hormone-and-skin theories in looksmaxxing communities center on the idea that androgens such as DHT, and drugs that change hormone levels such as anabolic steroids, drive acne, and that estrogen or anti-androgen approaches can offset it. Dermatology references do link androgens to acne: testosterone, DHT and DHEA increase sebum production, and DHT is described as the main hormonal driver of sebum .
Research on acne caused by steroids exists mainly for corticosteroids and in clinical settings such as transplant patients. A 1989 review described steroid acne as increasingly common with organ transplantation and cancer treatment .

name: Steroid back acne management

angle.text: Users of anabolic steroids or testosterone discuss back and shoulder acne as a side effect and look for ways to keep the skin clear while building physique. Acne is a recognised effect of these drugs; management advice is mostly general acne information.

summary: Back acne that people link to steroid use; reference material is limited to general acne and androgen information.
note: Severe acne is usually managed by clinicians; no dedicated trials found.
currentQuick:
Steroid back acne is acne on the back attributed to anabolic steroids or testosterone. It is a recurring topic in forum protocol discussions.
Thin sourcing is available here, so the article is short.
How it works: Androgens increase sebum production, which is linked to acne.
Risks and caveats: Anabolic steroids carry broader legal and health risks; standard acne treatments are listed by general references.
deepLead:
Steroid back acne (often called bacne in forums) refers to acne on the back and shoulders that people attribute to anabolic-androgenic steroid or testosterone use. Wikipedia states that anabolic-androgenic steroids and testosterone replacement can cause acne, and describes it as steroid acne .
The available reference material is limited to general acne information, and no published trial dedicated to back acne from performance-enhancing steroids was identified.

name: Sliding genioplasty

angle.text: Sliding genioplasty repositions the chin bone forward, back or sideways to reshape the chin and balance the profile. The result is visible after healing, and the evidence is mostly case series with few comparative trials.

summary: Cutting and moving the chin bone to reshape the chin; established surgery with case-series evidence and few comparative trials.
note: Reported effects include swelling and temporary lip numbness; nerve injury is rarer.
currentQuick:
Sliding genioplasty cuts the lower chin bone and repositions it, then fixes it with plates. It is used for chin projection, reduction, and feminization.
Evidence is mostly case series and reviews.
How it works: The cut bone segment moves to a new position and is fixed with plate and screws, altering chin shape using the patient's own bone.
Risks and caveats: Swelling, temporary numbness, infection, displacement and nerve damage have been reported; it does not correct bite.
deepLead:
Sliding genioplasty is a chin surgery in which a surgeon cuts the lower part of the chin bone and moves it forward, backward, vertically or sideways, then fixes it in place . Unlike an implant, it uses the patient's own bone.
It is used for cosmetic chin reshaping, in facial feminization, and as part of face-contouring and jaw surgery . On looksmaxxing forums it is discussed as a hardmaxxing option, often compared with chin implants .

name: Gonial angle reduction (V-line surgery)

angle.text: V-line surgery removes bone at the jaw angle to narrow the lower face into a tapered outline, often alongside chin reshaping. It is established in East Asian aesthetic surgery, with evidence mostly from surgeon case series.

summary: Surgical shaving of the lower jaw angle (and sometimes chin) to narrow the lower face; established in East Asian aesthetic surgery, evidence is mostly surgeon case series.
note: Major elective jaw surgery; the evidence base is largely surgeon-reported series rather than controlled trials.
currentQuick:
Gonial angle reduction removes bone from the corner of the lower jaw (the gonial angle) so that the face looks narrower and tapers toward the chin, the so-called V-line. It is often combined with chin reshaping (genioplasty) and is discussed in the aesthetic surgery literature mainly in the context of East Asian patients with wide lower faces.
In looksmaxxing forums it sits at the opposite end from jaw implants: instead of adding width and angularity, it removes them. Published evidence consists mainly of surgeon case descriptions and technique papers; no randomized trials were found.
How it works: Through incisions inside the mouth, the surgeon resects a portion of the mandibular angle, and in some designs also the outer cortex of the lower border, and may reshape the chin. A 1991 paper classified patients into types by the degree of angle protrusion and matched the amount of resection to each type. Botulinum toxin in the masseter muscle is a non-surgical alternative that some papers describe for slimming the lower face.
Risks and caveats: Reported risks of mandibular contouring in the literature include nerve injury, bleeding, infection, asymmetry and unsatisfactory contour; the Wikipedia article on facial feminization surgery names damage to the mental nerve as the greatest risk of jaw and chin reshaping. It is performed under general anesthesia and has a recovery period with swelling.
deepLead:
Gonial angle reduction, commonly marketed as V-line surgery, is a cosmetic jaw-contouring operation in which bone is removed from the angle of the mandible, where the lower border of the jaw meets the vertical ramus, in order to narrow the lower face and give it a tapered, V-shaped outline. It is frequently paired with reshaping of the chin.
The surgical literature on aesthetic mandibular contouring dates at least to a 1991 paper describing angle reduction and genioplasty for purely aesthetic reasons, which graded patients by the degree of angle protrusion. The topic appears in later work on Asian patients seeking a slimmer lower face, as well as in facial feminization surgery, where jaw reduction is one of several procedures used to soften a masculine lower face.
The evidence base consists mostly of technique descriptions and surgeon-reported case series; no randomized controlled trials were found. Reviews of the area note that surgical angle reduction is a complex procedure with significant risks and downtime, which has led some surgeons to describe less invasive options such as botulinum toxin injection into the masseter muscles.

name: Custom PEEK/Medpor jaw implants

angle.text: Patient-specific Medpor or PEEK implants add width or length to the jaw angle and ramus for a more defined lower face. The change is visible once swelling settles; published outcome data for purely cosmetic use is limited.

summary: Patient-specific implants designed from a CT scan to widen or lengthen the jaw and ramus; widely discussed online, with little published outcome data for purely cosmetic use.
note: Surgical implants placed on the facial skeleton; forum discussion centers on surgeon selection and design, and cosmetic-specific trial data were not found.
currentQuick:
Custom jaw implants are made for one person from a CT scan. The surgeon or a design team models the implant on a 3D copy of the patient's skull, and it is then manufactured, commonly in porous polyethylene (Medpor) or the polymer PEEK, and placed through the mouth. People use them to add width, height or projection to the jaw angle and ramus, often alongside chin and cheek implants.
On looksmaxxing forums, custom implants are a common alternative to jaw-moving surgery. Members trade names of surgeons, post design files and compare planned millimeter dimensions. Published clinical outcome data for cosmetic jaw implants specifically were not found among the sources reviewed.
How it works: The implant sits on the outside of the bone and adds volume. Forum designs described include a wrap-around implant that adds width at the jaw angle and height to the ramus and projection to the chin, with dimensions quoted in millimeters, for example a few millimeters of lateral projection and around 15 mm of vertical ramus height in one posted plan.
Risks and caveats: Risks of any facial implant include infection, displacement, asymmetry and nerve injury, and an implant can need removal. Forum posters stress that a wider jaw is not always more aesthetic and that design choices can produce a rounder rather than more angular jaw. No registered trials or published cosmetic outcome series were found in the sources used.
deepLead:
Custom jaw implants are patient-specific implants fabricated from a CT scan of the patient's facial skeleton to augment the jaw, typically at the gonial angle, the ramus, and sometimes the chin. Two materials are discussed most often in looksmaxxing communities: porous polyethylene, sold under the brand Medpor, and polyetheretherketone (PEEK), a rigid thermoplastic.
The topic is an almost entirely forum-driven one among the sources reviewed. Members of looksmax.org share lists of surgeons they regard as experienced in custom jaw work, post implant design files and discuss target ratios such as bigonial-to-bizygomatic width. No clinical trial or published case series specifically evaluating custom PEEK or Medpor implants for cosmetic jaw augmentation was found in the sources reviewed.

name: Ramus / vertical ramus augmentation

angle.text: Ramus augmentation, usually with a custom implant, adds height to the vertical part of the jaw for a longer, squarer jawline. The shape change is visible after healing, and very little cosmetic outcome data has been published.

summary: Adding height to the vertical part of the lower jaw, usually with a custom implant, for a longer and squarer jaw; essentially no published cosmetic outcome data.
note: Published ramus-implant literature concerns dental and reconstructive uses, not cosmetic augmentation.
currentQuick:
The ramus is the vertical branch of the lower jaw that rises from the jaw angle toward the ear. Vertical ramus augmentation means adding bone-surface volume there, in practice by placing an implant that raises the jaw angle, so the jawline looks longer and more defined from the side.
It is described in looksmaxxing circles as part of jaw implant design, often as one component of a custom wrap-around implant. The sources reviewed contain no published study of ramus augmentation for appearance; the medical literature on ramus implants concerns dental anchorage and reconstruction.
How it works: An implant is shaped to sit along the outer surface of the ramus and add height or width. In engineering studies of reconstruction, a ramus implant is fixed to the bone and the mechanical load transfer is analyzed.
Risks and caveats: Risks have not been studied for the cosmetic use. General implant risks discussed in surgery include infection, displacement and nerve injury near the jaw.
deepLead:
The mandibular ramus is the vertical portion of the lower jaw that connects the angle of the jaw to the joint near the ear. Ramus augmentation, or vertical ramus augmentation, refers to adding implant material along the ramus to increase its apparent height and the definition of the jaw angle, for a longer, squarer jawline.
Looksmaxxing communities discuss it mainly as one element of custom or wrap-around jaw implant designs. In the sources reviewed, the published literature on ramus implants addresses different questions: dental implants placed in the ramus area for denture support or orthodontic anchorage, and mechanical testing of implants used in jaw reconstruction. No study was found examining ramus augmentation for cosmetic purposes.

name: Mandibular advancement surgery (BSSO)

chain: Chin and jaw sit further forward
angle.text: BSSO moves the lower jaw forward and is used by looksmaxxers to improve a recessed lower third and side profile. It is a well-studied orthognathic operation for bite and function, usually combined with orthodontics.

summary: Established orthognathic operation that splits and moves the lower jaw forward; well studied for bite and function, and used by looksmaxxers to improve profile.
note: Major jaw surgery with a recognized risk of lasting numbness, relapse and joint changes; most research concerns functional rather than purely cosmetic outcomes.
currentQuick:
Bilateral sagittal split osteotomy (BSSO) is the standard operation for moving the lower jaw. The surgeon splits the jawbone lengthwise on each side behind the teeth, slides the tooth-bearing part forward and fixes it with plates and screws. It is used for recessed lower jaws, bite problems and some airway conditions, and is usually planned with an orthodontist.
In looksmaxxing communities it is a prominent hardmaxxing procedure, discussed alongside genioplasty, Le Fort upper-jaw surgery and implants as a way to improve the facial profile. Clinical research on BSSO is extensive, although most of it measures stability, nerve function and joint health rather than attractiveness.
How it works: Cuts are made through the mouth along the inner and outer cortex of the lower jaw, allowing the front segment to be advanced. Titanium plates or screws hold the new position while the bone heals, which the Wikipedia article on orthognathic surgery says takes several weeks with fuller remodeling over a few months.
Risks and caveats: Documented risks include numbness of the lower lip and chin from inferior alveolar nerve injury, relapse of the advancement, changes in the jaw joint including condylar resorption, swelling, infection, and a liquid-diet recovery period. Studies report that neurosensory disturbance can persist in a share of patients.
deepLead:
Mandibular advancement by bilateral sagittal split osteotomy (BSSO) is an orthognathic operation in which the lower jaw is cut along the ramus on each side, split, and the tooth-bearing segment is moved forward and fixed in the new position. It is the most commonly described procedure for repositioning the mandible and is usually combined with orthodontic treatment.
The operation is used medically for recessed lower jaws, bite problems, temporomandibular joint pathology and airway issues, and has a long clinical literature. Hugo Obwegeser is credited in the Wikipedia article on orthognathic surgery with developing the BSSO. In looksmaxxing communities, BSSO is discussed as a way to improve profile and jawline, often with genioplasty and with Le Fort I upper-jaw surgery in so-called bimax surgery.
Research on BSSO advancement addresses stability of the result, neurosensory disturbance, condylar remodeling and joint health, and patient well-being; the studies reviewed here are about function and surgical outcomes rather than perceived attractiveness.

name: FaceTite / Renuvion

angle.text: FaceTite and Renuvion are used to tighten loose skin and sharpen the jawline and neck without a facelift. Evidence is mostly case series, and the FDA has warned about off-label use.

summary: Subdermal radiofrequency (FaceTite) and helium-plasma (Renuvion) devices used to tighten the jawline and neck without a facelift; evidence is mostly case series, and the FDA has warned about off-label use.
note: The FDA has issued warnings about off-label Renuvion use and reported burns in adverse-event data; published studies are mainly retrospective.
currentQuick:
FaceTite and Renuvion are two different minimally invasive tightening technologies often mentioned together. FaceTite (made by InMode) places a small probe under the skin that delivers bipolar radiofrequency energy to heat fat and the underside of the skin; Renuvion (made by Apyx Medical, formerly Bovie) uses helium plasma with radiofrequency energy to heat and contract subdermal tissue.
They are used on the jawline, jowls and neck for patients with some laxity who are not ready for, or do not want, a facelift or neck lift. Published evidence is mostly retrospective reviews and case series, and no randomized trials were found among the sources reviewed.
How it works: Energy is delivered into the subdermal layer through small access points, heating adipose tissue and the dermis. The heat is intended to contract tissue and stimulate collagen remodeling, and the procedures are sometimes combined with liposuction or buccal fat pad removal.
Risks and caveats: Superficial burns, seromas, asymmetry and pigmentation changes are the most common complications described for Renuvion, with rarer infection, nerve damage and scarring. The FDA has warned against off-label use, and a 2026 surgical paper discusses fibrosis, fat loss and added complexity when patients later undergo neck lift after nonsurgical treatments.
deepLead:
FaceTite and Renuvion are minimally invasive devices for tightening loose skin and contouring the lower face and neck. FaceTite, from InMode, delivers bipolar radiofrequency energy to the subdermal space through a small probe; Renuvion, which grew out of the J-Plasma system from Apyx Medical (formerly Bovie Medical), uses helium plasma energy to heat and contract subdermal soft tissue.
They are discussed as options in what surgeons call the treatment gap: patients with laxity too severe for traditional noninvasive devices but not severe enough to justify an excisional operation. Published studies are largely retrospective reviews and descriptive case series, often reporting FaceTite combined with fractional radiofrequency or liposuction.
The FDA has cleared Renuvion for specific indications and has warned against off-label uses, citing reports of burns and tissue damage.

name: Morpheus8 (RF microneedling)

chain: Tighter skin on jaw and neck
angle.text: Morpheus8 is promoted for tightening skin and remodeling fat along the jawline and neck. Its evidence comes mainly from case series and reviews.

summary: InMode fractional radiofrequency microneedling device marketed for skin tightening and subdermal fat remodeling along the jawline and neck; evidence is mainly case series and reviews.
note: Grokipedia reports the FDA has noted risks such as burns, scarring and unintended fat loss with RF microneedling; a 2026 paper describes fibrosis and surgical complexity after nonsurgical treatments.
currentQuick:
Morpheus8 is a handheld device from InMode that combines microneedling with bipolar radiofrequency (RF) energy. Needles penetrate the skin to set depths and deliver heat to the dermis and subdermal layers, with the stated aims of stimulating collagen, tightening skin and remodeling a small amount of fat.
It is used on the face and neck, including the jawline and jowls, as a lower-downtime option for mild to moderate laxity. Reviews and retrospective series report improvements, but no randomized comparison against surgery was found in the sources reviewed.
How it works: Insulated microneedles create channels in the skin while RF energy heats tissue at depths that Grokipedia says reach up to 8 mm. The resulting controlled injury is described as triggering a healing response with new collagen, and deeper settings are said to coagulate subdermal fat. It is often combined with FaceTite or liposuction.
Risks and caveats: Described risks include burns, scarring, pigmentation changes and unintended fat loss. A 2026 surgical paper reports that fibrosis and fat loss after nonsurgical treatments can complicate later neck lift surgery.
deepLead:
Morpheus8 is a fractional radiofrequency microneedling device made by InMode that combines microneedles with bipolar RF energy to heat the dermis and subdermal tissue. Manufacturers and practitioners describe it as promoting collagen production, tightening skin and remodeling adipose tissue on the face, neck and body.
It grew out of InMode's Fractora fractional RF platform; a 2020 study describes a combination of FaceTite bipolar RF and a fractional bipolar RF device (Fractora modified to Morpheus8) for lower face and neck laxity. Grokipedia, an AI-generated source, reports commercial introduction around 2018, US FDA clearance in 2020 for electrocoagulation and hemostasis, and a further clearance in 2024 for soft tissue contraction.
Reviews in dermatology and facial plastic surgery present RF microneedling as a minimally invasive option for skin laxity, acne scarring and rejuvenation, while the published evidence on jawline and fat remodeling consists largely of retrospective series and combination reports.

name: Hard-food diet (tough foods)

angle.text: Followers chew raw carrots, tough meats and similar foods in the belief that it improves jaw and facial development. No human trial has shown that it changes jaw shape.

summary: Eating tough, fibrous foods to load the jaw; no human trial shows it changes jaw shape.
note: Hard foods are listed among suggested parafunctions in jaw-pain literature.
currentQuick:
The hard-food diet means eating tough, fibrous foods, such as raw vegetables or chewy meat, to give the jaw muscles more work. Followers hope this builds a stronger jaw or better facial development.
The chewing muscles do adapt to use, but no published human trial located for this entry has tested whether harder foods change adult jaw or facial appearance.
How it works: Chewing effort is meant to load the masseter and related muscles. Reference sources describe heavy habitual use such as clenching or constant gum chewing as able to enlarge the masseter.
Risks and caveats: Jaw-pain literature lists very hard foods among suggested parafunctional habits that may contribute to temporomandibular symptoms, though the link is debated.
deepLead:
The hard-food diet, also called tough-food chewing or "ancestral chewing", is a practice in which people deliberately eat fibrous or hard foods such as raw carrots, tough meats or similar items, with the aim of loading the jaw muscles and, in believers' accounts, improving jaw and facial development.
Chewing is driven by a motor program that adapts to the type of food being eaten, and the masseter, the main jaw-closing muscle, can enlarge in response to heavy use such as clenching, grinding or constant gum chewing. Whether eating harder foods in adulthood changes the visible shape of the jaw or face has not been established in published human trials located for this entry.
The practice is discussed in looksmaxxing circles alongside mewing and jaw exercises, which health bodies and orthodontic organizations have described as lacking supporting evidence.

name: Jaw-chewing with Falim gum 8 hours

angle.text: Users chew Falim gum for hours a day to enlarge the masseter and widen the lower face. Muscle growth from chewing is plausible; the aesthetic results of such long sessions are anecdotal, and forum posters report jaw pain.

summary: Hard-gum chewing for hours to bulk the masseter; muscle growth is plausible, jaw pain is reported.
note: Users report jaw pain and clicking; overgrowth of the masseter is documented with constant gum chewing.
currentQuick:
People chew very hard Turkish gum such as Falim for many hours daily, aiming for a bigger, wider masseter and stronger-looking jaw.
The muscle can enlarge with constant gum chewing, but no trial has tested the practice for appearance. Users report both gains and pain.
How it works: Repetitive heavy chewing loads the masseter, which can hypertrophy with heavy use.
Risks and caveats: Reported effects include jaw pain, popping, ear-area pressure and excess masseter bulk. Temporomandibular literature lists gum chewing as a suggested but unproven contributor to jaw problems.
deepLead:
Extended Falim chewing is a practice in looksmaxxing communities in which people chew Falim, a hard Turkish gum, for hours a day, in some accounts up to eight, to enlarge the masseter and widen or strengthen the lower face.
The masseter is known to enlarge with heavy use; clinical descriptions list clenching, bruxism and constant gum chewing as causes of masseter hypertrophy, which can change facial shape and is sometimes linked to temporomandibular joint problems. Forum users describe both enlargement they welcome and jaw pain they attribute to long sessions.
No clinical trial of marathon chewing for appearance was located for this entry.

name: Chin strap while sleeping

angle.text: Users wear chin straps during sleep to encourage nasal breathing and a closed-mouth resting posture, often alongside mewing or mouth taping. The link to facial reshaping is anecdotal and untested.

summary: A strap to keep the mouth shut overnight; no evidence it reshapes the face.
note: Not studied for appearance; nasal obstruction causes of mouth breathing are medical matters.
currentQuick:
A chin strap holds the mouth closed during sleep. Followers say it promotes nasal breathing and better jaw posture.
No published trial located for this entry has tested it for facial appearance.
How it works: It mechanically prevents the jaw dropping open while asleep.
Risks and caveats: Mouth breathing usually reflects nasal congestion, and reference sources advise treating the cause. Health effects of related mouth taping are described as little researched.
deepLead:
A chin strap worn during sleep is a band that holds the mouth closed overnight. In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed as a way to encourage nasal breathing and a closed-mouth resting posture, sometimes alongside mewing or mouth taping.
Reference sources note that chronic mouth breathing in children is associated with dental and facial changes such as a long, narrow face, and that the health effects of mouth taping have been little researched. No trial located for this entry has tested chin straps for appearance.

name: Myofunctional therapy

angle.text: Myofunctional therapy is used clinically for sleep apnea and tongue dysfunction, and looksmaxxing communities discuss it for tongue posture and jaw development. The facial-appearance use is untested.

summary: Tongue and mouth exercises with sleep-apnea evidence; no evidence it changes facial looks.
note: Evidence is for airway outcomes, not appearance.
currentQuick:
Myofunctional therapy is a set of tongue, lip and throat exercises used clinically for sleep apnea, tongue dysfunction and open bite. Looksmaxxers discuss it alongside tongue posture and mewing.
Systematic reviews exist for sleep apnea; none located tests it for facial appearance.
How it works: Exercises aim to change tone and function of the upper airway and oral muscles.
Risks and caveats: No notable risks are described in the sources consulted. Sleep apnea is a medical condition managed by clinicians.
deepLead:
Orofacial myofunctional therapy (OMT) is a program of exercises for the tongue, lips, cheeks and throat muscles, used clinically for conditions such as obstructive sleep apnea, tongue dysfunction and open bite, and discussed in looksmaxxing communities in connection with tongue posture and jaw development.
A systematic review and meta-analysis of myofunctional therapy for obstructive sleep apnea examined polysomnographic, snoring and sleepiness outcomes in children and adults. Further studies examine its use alongside CPAP, in children with sleep-disordered breathing, and in orthodontic cases. Evidence concerns airway and function; no trial located for this entry has tested it for facial appearance.

name: Jaw contouring makeup (contour/highlight)

angle.text: Contour and highlight makeup makes the jawline look more defined for photos, video and events. The effect is visible as soon as it is blended and lasts until removed.

summary: Shading and highlighting to fake a sharper jawline; temporary and cosmetic.
note: Cosmetic illusion only; no studies of jawline-specific effects found.
currentQuick:
Jaw contouring uses darker and lighter makeup to suggest a more defined jaw. It is the same shading idea used for cheekbones and noses.
It is temporary and works as an optical effect.
How it works: Darker shades read as shadow and lighter shades as raised areas, changing perceived shape.
Risks and caveats: The sources consulted do not discuss risks.
deepLead:
Jaw contouring is the use of makeup shading and highlighting to make the jawline look more defined. It applies the general technique of contouring, in which a shade darker than the skin creates apparent shadow and a lighter shade brings areas forward.
The technique has a long theatrical and film history and became mainstream in the 2010s through celebrity and social media use. It is temporary and cosmetic.

name: Neck tension / platysma flex

angle.text: Posers flex the platysma to make the jaw-neck transition look more defined in photos and mirror checks. The effect is visible while the muscle is tensed; it is a posing habit rather than something studied.

summary: Tensing the neck muscle for a sharper jaw-neck line in photos; a posing habit with no studies behind it.
note: Temporary visual effect only while flexed; no trials exist.
currentQuick:
Platysma flexing means deliberately tightening the thin muscle across the front of the neck so the area under the jaw looks more defined, usually for a photo.
It is discussed as a posing technique rather than a lasting change. No published studies have examined it.
How it works: The platysma sits just under the skin of the neck; contracting it tightens and wrinkles the overlying skin and can pull the lower lip and mouth corners downward [1].
Risks and caveats: No specific harms have been documented for the practice. Clinical sources note that prominent platysmal bands can be aggravated by some activities such as weightlifting [1]. No trials exist.
deepLead:
Neck tension or platysma flexing is a practice in looksmaxxing communities in which a person deliberately contracts the platysma, the thin superficial muscle of the neck, to make the jaw-neck transition and lower jawline look more defined, mostly for photographs or mirror checks.
The platysma is a broad, thin sheet that overlies the sternocleidomastoid. When it contracts it wrinkles the neck skin slightly and can pull down the lower lip and mouth corners . Its visible bands become more noticeable with age and can be aggravated by weightlifting and some facelift procedures .
No published clinical studies have been found that test platysma flexing or neck exercises for jawline appearance.

name: Lower face rejuvenation filler (jowl filler)

angle.text: Filler along the pre-jowl and marionette areas is used to smooth the lower face and restore the line of the jaw. The result is visible right after injection; jowl-specific trial data is thin.

summary: Filler placed along the pre-jowl and marionette lines to smooth the lower face; established aesthetic medicine with thin jowl-specific trial data.
note: Rare vascular complications can cause permanent harm.
currentQuick:
Jowl filler is the use of injectable dermal filler, most often hyaluronic acid, to fill the hollow in front of the jowl and the marionette area so the jaw line looks smoother.
It is a mainstream aesthetic procedure; trials focused on jowls are few and small.
How it works: The filler adds volume under the skin. Hyaluronic acid products are usually cross-linked for stability [1].
Risks and caveats: Bruising and redness are common. Embolisation can cause blindness or skin necrosis in rare cases [1]. Fillers are regulated as medical devices [1].
deepLead:
Jowl filler refers to injecting dermal filler into the pre-jowl, marionette and lower-face areas to restore lost volume and smooth the line of the jaw.
Dermal fillers are substances injected into connective tissue; hyaluronic acid is the most common material, and fillers are used for wrinkles, volume loss and enhancement of the lips, cheeks and jawline . Common side effects include bruising, redness and pain; rare vascular complications can cause permanent vision loss or skin necrosis .
Clinical research specific to jowls is small: one registered trial of fillers for jowl improvement enrolled 16 participants .

name: Jaw expansion via MSE / SARPE

angle.text: SARPE and MSE widen the upper jaw in adults and are discussed in forums for facial width, cheek fullness and bite, often alongside braces or jaw surgery. They are established orthodontic procedures with documented complications.

summary: Surgical or mini-implant jaw widening for adults; real orthodontic procedures with documented complications, discussed in forums as a facial-width tool.
note: Surgery with documented complications including rare haemorrhage.
currentQuick:
SARPE and MSE are ways to widen the upper jaw in adults. SARPE uses surgery to free the palate; MSE uses mini-implants to anchor an expander.
They are established orthodontic treatments for transverse deficiency, and forums discuss them for appearance.
How it works: An expander applies force across the midpalatal suture, after surgical release in SARPE or via bone anchors in MSE/MARPE [1].
Risks and caveats: Reported problems include pain, relapse, periodontal effects and rare life-threatening haemorrhage [1][4][7].
deepLead:
SARPE (surgically assisted rapid palatal expansion) and MSE (miniscrew-assisted or maxillary skeletal expander) are ways of widening the upper jaw in adults whose palatal suture has fused. Looksmaxxing communities discuss them for facial width and bite, often alongside braces or bimaxillary surgery.
In SARPE a surgeon cuts the midpalatal suture and an expander is then activated by an orthodontist . MARPE anchors the expander with mini-implants for skeletal expansion without surgery, though most adult men may still need a surgical assist . A literature review described SARPE as having gradually gained popularity for adults with maxillary transverse deficiency .
Studies describe complications and some relapse; haemorrhage has been reported in rare cases .

name: Braces / orthodontics for jaw shape

angle.text: Braces are used to align teeth and bite, and in looksmaxxing circles to improve profile, especially combined with jaw surgery. Orthodontics is established dental treatment that can change the profile somewhat.

summary: Established dental treatment for bite and tooth position that can change profile somewhat, especially combined with jaw surgery.
note: Facial-aesthetic outcomes are less studied than dental ones; relapse is common without retainers.
currentQuick:
Braces and other orthodontic appliances move teeth and, in growing patients, guide jaws. People interested in appearance discuss them for bite and profile.
Severe jaw discrepancies may need surgery combined with orthodontics.
How it works: Appliances apply sustained force to move teeth through bone; palatal expanders and headgear act on jaw alignment [1].
Risks and caveats: Decalcification and decay with poor hygiene, and frequent relapse, are described; retainers are often recommended [1].
deepLead:
Orthodontics is the dental specialty that diagnoses and corrects misaligned teeth, jaws and bite patterns, and can modify facial growth; braces are its best-known tool . In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed as a way to improve bite and facial profile, often alongside jaw surgery.
Wikipedia notes that clinicians learned that perfect occlusion alone does not ensure good facial appearance, and that headgear and palatal expansion can alter jaw alignment or airflow . Severe malocclusions may need jaw surgery followed by orthodontics .
Registered trials in the area mostly address alignment speed, sleep and airway, rather than facial attractiveness.

name: PRF / PRP face contouring

angle.text: PRF and PRP made from a patient's own blood are used in aesthetic clinics to add facial volume and improve skin quality. They are used in clinics for skin, but true contouring has not been trialled.

summary: Blood-derived concentrates injected for facial skin and volume; used in aesthetic clinics, with no trials of true contouring.
note: Preparation varies by clinic; infection control matters.
currentQuick:
PRP and PRF are made by spinning a person's own blood to concentrate platelets and growth factors, then injecting or applying them to the face.
They are marketed for skin rejuvenation; evidence overall is described as mixed.
How it works: Platelets release growth factors thought to stimulate tissue repair [1].
Risks and caveats: Adverse effects are generally low, though improper equipment reuse caused a 2024 HIV cluster at an unlicensed spa [1].
deepLead:
PRF and PRP face contouring refers to using platelet-rich plasma or platelet-rich fibrin, concentrates made from a patient's own blood, to add volume or improve the skin of the face.
Platelet-rich plasma is a blood fraction with platelet levels typically 3 to 5 times normal, believed to release growth factors that aid healing . Aesthetic clinics use it for wrinkles and fine lines, often with microneedling in "vampire facials" . Wikipedia describes the evidence overall as mixed .
Registered trials of platelet-rich fibrin focus on dental and nerve applications; a small trial of PRF in a face cream is the nearest to cosmetic use .

name: Tongue pressing against roof (tongue push-ups)

angle.text: Tongue push-ups are a forceful mewing variant in which people press the tongue against the roof of the mouth, aiming to reshape the jaws and face. The facial-change claim has no studies behind it.

summary: A more forceful mewing variant; tongue presses on the palate, with no studies behind the facial-change claim.
note: Orthodontic bodies say mewing lacks evidence of jaw change.
currentQuick:
Tongue push-ups are a variation on mewing where the tongue is pressed against the roof of the mouth, sometimes in timed holds.
Proponents say it shapes the jaw; the American Association of Orthodontists says there is no evidence mewing improves the jaw [1].
How it works: The theory is that tongue pressure on the palate guides upper jaw growth or shape. No studies have tested this for the specific exercise.
Risks and caveats: No specific harms have been documented for the exercise. The mewing page notes that its originator Mike Mew was struck from the UK dental register in 2024 after a misconduct hearing involving child patients [1].
deepLead:
Tongue push-ups are a variant of mewing in which a person presses the tongue firmly against the roof of the mouth, sometimes in repeated holds, in the belief that this reshapes the jaws and face.
Mewing itself is described as an unproven form of oral posture training associated with the orthotropics practice of British orthodontist John Mew and his son Mike Mew . The American Association of Orthodontists has stated there is no evidence that mewing improves the jaw .
No studies were found that test tongue push-ups specifically.
